title: Wren Street Ensemble | Notes on next month’s concert
titleZh: 鷦鷯街樂團｜下個月音樂會的備忘
passage:
When we describe a first performance, be clear about what is new. A piece of music and an arrangement of that piece are not the same thing: an arrangement changes how the music is played, although the original tune remains. We should name a previous public performance if it helps readers understand why the tune may sound familiar. We can call an arrangement a premiere only if that particular arrangement has never been performed in public.

People may remember Under the Lantern from last year’s library concert, where our trio played it. Our conductor has since written a five-player arrangement. The five of us played through its full score in a rehearsal closed to visitors; the version has not been heard at any public event. I know someone has already drafted the headline ‘A tune you’ve never heard’ for the programme. Please leave room for the people who remember it.

The hall manager has asked us to keep a long pause in the middle of River Steps. The unexpected silence is part of the music, and the conductor does not want to replace it with a spoken cue. We can, however, tell listeners where the whole piece ends without telling them exactly when the silence starts; they need a reason to stay attentive through that silence, not a warning that spoils its effect.

After the open rehearsal, several listeners said they had taken the silence for the end. There were two descriptions in the handout. The short headline called the silence the ending; the smaller note correctly described the final solo that follows it. The volunteers distributing the handout noticed that many readers glanced at only the headline. We will keep the smaller note for people who want the extra detail.
passageZh:
介紹首演時，要說清楚新的是什麼。一首樂曲和它的改編版本並不是同一件事：改編會改變演奏方式，但原有旋律仍保留。如果提及先前的公開演出，有助於解釋為什麼聽眾可能覺得旋律熟悉，我們應在節目單上寫明。只有從未公開演出過的特定改編版本，才可以稱作首演。

有人也許記得去年的圖書館音樂會上，本團三重奏曾演奏〈燈籠下〉。此後指揮為它寫了五人改編版。我們五人曾在不開放訪客的排練中完整演奏過譜上的內容，但這版本還沒在任何公開活動中演出。我知道有人已把「你從沒聽過的旋律」寫成節目單標題草稿。請也顧及那些還記得這首曲子的人。

場館經理請我們保留〈河畔階梯〉中段的一段長停頓。這段出乎意料的安靜是樂曲的一部分，指揮不想用口頭提示取代它。不過，我們可以告訴聽眾整首曲子在哪裡結束，不必明說安靜會在何時開始；他們需要的是在停頓時繼續聽下去的依據，而不是破壞效果的預告。

開放排練後，有幾位聽眾說他們以為安靜就代表結束。講義上有兩處說明：簡短的標題把安靜說成終點；較小字的附註則正確描述了安靜之後的最後一段獨奏。發講義的志工發現，許多讀者只瞄了標題。我們會保留小字附註，供想多了解的人閱讀。
